result.markdown: --- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Graph.get_selected_edge_ids()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: Get currently selected edge IDs. twitter-card: title: >- [Graph.get_selected_edge_ids()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: Get currently selected edge IDs. title: >- [Graph.get_selected_edge_ids()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: Get currently selected edge IDs. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Get currently selected edge IDs. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L24622-L24686){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature Graph.get_selected_edge_ids() ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Get selected edge ids](../assets/graphs/get-selected-edge-ids.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="A grid whose edges are labeled with their ids 1 to 7, with edges 1, 4, and 7 (A–B, B–E, E–F) selected in the accent color. get_selected_edge_ids() returns the list of those ids, 7, 4, 1, in no guaranteed order." width="100%"} Returns the IDs of the edges that are currently in the edge selection, as built up by the edge `select_*`, `deselect_edges()`, and `invert_edge_selection()` methods (and the edge-producing traversals such as `trav_out_edge()`). It is a read-only view: calling it does not change the selection. Use it to inspect what a selection rule matched, to look up the selected edges with `get_edge()`, or to save a selection and restore it later with `select_edges_by_id()`. The selection is stored as a set, so the order of the returned IDs is arbitrary; sort the list if you need a stable order. If you only need the number of selected edges, `count_selected_edges()` avoids building the list. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [list[int]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : List of selected edge IDs in no particular order, empty if no edges are selected. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Selecting the edges heavier than `0.5` returns the IDs of the second and third edges, `2` and `3` (edge IDs follow creation order): ::: {#edacbaa2 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_nodes(["A", "B", "C", "D"]) .add_edges([("A", "B", 0.3), ("B", "C", 0.8), ("C", "D", 0.6)]) .select_edges(lambda e: e.weight > 0.5) ) sorted(graph.get_selected_edge_ids()) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` [2, 3] ``` ::: ::: Each ID can be resolved back to its `Edge` object, here to list the endpoints of the selected edges by label: ::: {#ca03a8fa .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} [ (graph.get_label_from_id(e.source), graph.get_label_from_id(e.target)) for e in (graph.get_edge(eid) for eid in sorted(graph.get_selected_edge_ids())) ] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` [('B', 'C'), ('C', 'D')] ``` ::: ::: When a predicate matches nothing, the result is an empty list. This cycle was created without explicit edge weights, so every edge's `weight` is `None` and no edge passes: ::: {#05759ba8 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_cycle_graph(4) .select_edges(lambda e: e.weight is not None and e.weight > 0.5) ) graph.get_selected_edge_ids() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` [] ``` ::: :::
